 Live .  44,660 viewing 44660 viewing Live page Updated 1 minute ago Antonelli bids to clinch title as Leclerc leads early stages of Mexico City Grand Prix
 Mexican Grand Prix
 BBC Radio 5 Live
 Close Mexican Grand Prix
 BBC Radio 5 Live
 Listen live Live Reporting (active) 
 Leaderboard 
 Summary
 Leclerc leads Mexico City Grand Prix as Hamilton drops to third
 Antonelli will become world champion with ninth place - he is currently running in fourth
 Mercedes driver will also clinch title if neither Hamilton nor Russell win race - full permutations here 
 Italian Antonelli, 20, would be youngest title winner in Formula 1 history
 Benson Q&A: Send us your questions 
 Close form Send us your F1 views
 Get involved Live Reporting
 Lorraine McKenna
 Post published at 20:23 GMT 20:23 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Charles is comfortably in the lead but I saw him going into Turn One and he had a bit of a drift going into Turn One as he put the lock on, we will be wanting to see how long his tyres are going to last. They should have a good few laps in them. When you have used tyres they don't seem to fire up quite as quickly as the new tyres.
 1 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Five-second time penalty for Leclerc published at 20:22 GMT 20:22 GMT 
 Lap 13/71 
 The stewards have delivered their verdict, and it's a five-second time penalty for Charles Leclerc for leaving the track and gaining an advantage. 
 George Russell was also under the spotlight for his contact with Isack Hadjar. The stewards' decision on that one is a 10-second penalty for the Mercedes man for causing a collision. 
 Leclerc leads, Russell is in fifth. 
 231 58 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 20:21 GMT 20:21 GMT 
 Select the 'Get Involved' button to have your say 
 Fed up with Leclerc’s lack of team discipline. Ferrari need to get rid of one or the other of their drivers.
 Stu, Chesterfield 
 759 172 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:20 GMT 20:20 GMT 
 Lap 12/71 
 Max Verstappen has called into to say he's not got the best grip on these medium tyres. Over at McLaren, Lando Norris is told Plan A is probably the way to go. 
 For Oscar Piastri, who was knocked out in Q2 yesterday, he's made his way into the points and up to seventh. 
 110 18 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:19 GMT 20:19 GMT 
 Marc Priestley 
Former F1 mechanic on Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Charles Leclerc ran off the track and clearly gained a massive advantage. Not only did he hold his position having got around the outside of Lewis Hamilton, you can even argue that he made the overtake off the race track. The stewards will frown upon that.
 471 65 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:19 GMT 20:19 GMT 
 Lap 11/71 
 Charles Leclerc has increased his gap to Max Verstappen to about two seconds over Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who opted to. start on medium at lights out. 
 Sergio Perez, in front of his adoring home fans, has climbed all the way up to 14th in the Cadillac. 
 86 39 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:18 GMT 20:18 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Charles has been making noise all day long about how difficult it was going to be to pass. He had in his mind that you absolutely have to get to the front of the race and he has got himself in the front but he might have incurred this penalty. 
 The problem is you can't instigate an instruction for a guy at Ferrari to fall back behind Max Verstappen. Isn't he supposed to fall back behind Lewis?
 256 39 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:18 GMT 20:18 GMT 
 Lap 9/71 
 The virtual safety car is cleared and we're racing again in Mexico. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is closing in on Lewis Hamilton, who is on used soft tyres. The Italian would love a podium to cap off his championship-winning (as it stands) weekend. 
 68 38 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:17 GMT 20:17 GMT 
 Lap 8/71 
 Turn Four was the flashpoint for Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton,which is still under investigation by the stewards. The Monegasque driver was on the outside of Hamilton and both end up off the track. 
 George Russell fell apart at lights out, and the Mercedes driver also made contact with Isack Hadjar's Red Bull, sending the Frenchman spinning out and down to the back of the field. 
 52 75 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Virtual safety car published at 20:14 GMT 20:14 GMT 
 Lap 7/71 
 It's turned into a miserable day for Aston Martin, who now ask Fernando Alonso's team-mate Lance Stroll to pull over and stop the car. The Canadian does as he's told, and the virtual safety car is deployed. 
 Charles Leclerc leads, Max Verstappen is 1.2 seconds behind and Lewis Hamilton, who started on pole, is third. 
 80 227 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:12 GMT 20:12 GMT 
 Lap 6/71 
 Fernando Alonso joked after qualifying he was heading to Brazil following another disappointment on Saturday. He did start the race today, but now he's being asked to retire the car by Aston Martin. 
 57 282 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:11 GMT 20:11 GMT 
 Lap 5/71 
 Race leader Charles Leclerc is 1.7 seconds ahead of the red Bull of Max Verstappen, but the Monegasque driver is under investigation for his fight with Lewis Hamilton, who is running in third spot, ahead of Kimi Antonelli. 
 180 72 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Hamilton to Ferrari published at 20:10 GMT 20:10 GMT 
 Hamilton: "What's happening about Charles?"
 Team engineer: "Investigation ongoing and they will let you know."
 322 77 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:10 GMT 20:10 GMT 
 Damon Hill 
1996 world champion on BBC Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 Ferrari are not going to be pleased in asking the stewards to look into the challenge there on the Ferraris because if they give a penalty to Charles, then Max is in the front of the race.
 179 74 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:10 GMT 20:10 GMT 
 Lap 4/71 
 The stewards think the Charles Leclerc-Lewis Hamilton intra-team battle needs investigating. The seven-time world champion then comes on the radio to ask his pit wall what's going on? 
 Lando Norris also lost out during the first-lap tussles but now the world champion is up to seventh place after overtaking Franco Colapinto. 
 Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is fourth. 
 121 25 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Hamilton to Ferrari published at 20:09 GMT 20:09 GMT 
 Hamilton: "Got pushed out by my own team-mate."
 507 248 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:09 GMT 20:09 GMT 
 Lap 3/71 
 Lewis Hamilton also went off the track in that scrap with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, so let's see what the race control makes of that incident. 
 George Russell has passed Arvid Lindblad and is now running in fifth place, while Franco Colapinto has climbed from 11th to seventh in the Alpine. 
 100 33 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 20:08 GMT 20:08 GMT 
 Marc Priestley 
Former F1 mechanic on Radio 5 Live in Mexico City 
 We said it was going to be chaos and that is exactly what happened. But it was the two Ferraris going wheel to wheel, they didn't give each other an inch. Lewis Hamilton, I'm sure will be furious with his team-mate, they pushed each other all around the outside. 
 240 82 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Leclerc leads from Verstappen published at 20:07 GMT 20:07 GMT 
 Lap 2/71 
 Isack Hadjar was spun round on that opening lap and has now tumbled down the field and is behind pit-lane starter Liam Lawson. 
 Max Verstappen thinks Charles Leclerc should be giving the position back, while Lewis Hamilton is adamant his team-mate pushed him off the track. 
 220 89 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Team radio - Verstappen to Red Bull published at 20:06 GMT 20:06 GMT 
 Verstappen: "Charles has to give that position"
